source.author: lemoussel
source.text: In this project, I built a simple vectorless RAG workflow using **PageIndex** and **Hermes Agent**. Instead of splitting documents into chunks and retrieving them through vector similarity, the system relies on a **hierarchical document structure** and **tool-based reasoning**. The agent first understands how the document is organized, then decides which pages to inspect before answering.

review.reason: The distinctive mechanism is a persistent discussion-only state enforced by blocking tool calls at the hook level, with a second command that resumes execution carrying the conversation forward. Documentation describes /plan, which writes an implementation plan instead of executing a single request, and documents hooks and slash commands as plugin capabilities, but not a hook-enforced no-execution mode with a resume command.

closestDocs.excerpt: (Plan mode works the same way but is a built-in command now: `/plan [request]` tells Hermes to inspect context if needed, write a markdown implementation plan instead of executing the task, and save the result under `.hermes/plans/` relative to the active workspace/backend working directory.)
closestDocs.distinction: /plan produces a markdown plan for one request and stops; it is not a mode that stays on across turns, blocks every tool at the hook level, and is lifted by a second command that keeps the discussion in context.

source.author: ogiberstein
source.text:
- My 'main agent' is my 'Chief of Staff'  who has his own memory cross-project/workflow. We have a weekly process to prune this memory for it to remain high-level
- We have a soul.md with focus on how we work together
- Every 'project' (1 project = 1 Slack channel) has its own agent sub-profile with its own memory. Each agent maintains his own memory file. Sometimes they still write random stuff into memory but mostly it works nowadays. 
- The weekly memory cleanup goes through each memory file to audit it against our 'principles of what belongs into each profile's memory'
- The whole system runs on VPS (I use Hostinger) and over time I have set up various hardening processes to make sure that if the main model fails, we have a backup routing in place + we have a backup of the whole agent operating system that gets backed up every night to Github 
- We use Obsidian as a recording system for projects & processes that both the agent/sub-agents and me access
- Daily reporting is sent to Whatsapp. All 'operational level' stuff gets discussed with 'Chief of Staff' agent. I have a 'Brain' channel where the 'Project Manager' lives with whom I discuss cross-project things. Each channel has its own 'Product Owner'
- I am also setting up something similar for investing/trading with a 'CIO'
- I also have Claude Code set up on the VPS. Hermes has a skill to use Claude so I get it to use Claude to audit its own code. For complex stuff I still sometimes use Claude Code locally on my laptop but sync up with Hermes via Github
- Every so often I will use GPT 5.4 Pro with Extended Thinking (connected to Github) to also audit code and prepare .md files which I drop into repos for fixing. Goal here: have as many independent models/sessions/prompts have a 'fresh' look at it. It's a feedback loop that tends to improve code quality quite significantly
